newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo industries propel Egypt bourse turnover.
newsitem.headline: Cairo industries propel Egypt bourse turnover.

text.p: Turnover on the Cairo bourse was propelled to above average levels on Wednesday mostly by activity in Cairo Precision Industries and Cairo Light Industries shares, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said.
The CMA report said the index closed at 370.72 points. On Tuesday it said the index finished at 368.24 points.

Wednesday's volume was 86.66 million pounds ($25.5 million) with Cairo Precision scooping up 10.85 million pounds worth of turnover in four transactions. Its share gained 6.5 pounds to close at 136.5.
Sister company Cairo Light Industries turnover was higher at 16 million pounds, but the price closed down 15 pounds at 286.
"It was apparently all arranged within the company," said Ihab al-Mahlawi of Intercapital brokerage. "I think a stake from the company was being sold to retail clients through a brokerage."
Egyptian Financial and Industrial was also notable. "It traded quite big volumes," said Mahlawi.
Its share price climbed 3.45 pounds to close at 209.15 in turnover worth 5.46 million.
Amriyah Cement edged up 0.75 pounds to close at 84.75 pounds in volume worth 4.27 million pounds.
"When it (share price) went to 84, it became very attractive," said Mahlawi.

Medinet Nasr Housing and Development announced in a published statement on Wednesday that 1996/97 third quarter pre-tax profit was up at 156.377 million pounds. Its share closed unchanged at 490 in trade worth 2.5 million pounds.
Brokers have said trade in that stock was probably generated by investor anticipation of its forthcoming one-for-one free share offer. Authorities approved the split last month.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 524.78 points from 529 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms rose to 269.56 from 265.68.
Out of the 94 shares traded, 32 ended up, 38 fell and 24 were unchanged.
